newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN SAYS H2 REVENUES MIGHT TIGHTEN.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN SAYS H2 REVENUES MIGHT TIGHTEN.

text.p: Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik told parliament on Wednesday that the country's first-half 1996 budget deficit of 6.13 billion crowns was satisfactory, but revenues might get tighter later in the year.

Last month, Kozlik's ministry reported total revenue of 79.5 billion crowns, with expenditures of 85.7 billion crowns, representing 49 percent and 45.2 percent respectively of the total budget for 1996.
"These results are satisfactory with regards to the deficit," Kozlik told the house on Wednesday.
The budget deficit for the entire year was forecast at 27 billion crowns, with the budget revenues expected to total 162.4 billion crowns and expenditures 189.4 billion crowns.
Kozlik did not offer a revised forecast for the budget for the full year.

He said the biggest shortfall on expected revenues in the first half of the year came in the value-added tax -- totalling about 6.4 billion crowns -- and the sales tax, representing around 2.3 billion crowns.
"From this point of view, the development of the growth of the budget income will be tight in the second half of the year," Kozlik said.
He said if the negative tendencies in revenues from the taxes continued in the second half of the year, the shortfall on these revenues alone could total some 10 billion crowns.
